note: HAND-AUTHORED (PERF-04, issue #471) — the one file in internal/perfbench that is NOT generated. A budget is a governance decision, not a measurement. The deterministic budget (query count, rows touched) is the committed baseline.json / datamovement-baseline.json itself, re-asserted here from the budget vocabulary and gated per PR. `max_wall_ms` is a hard ceiling on the median at anchor_profile for operations on an interactive path — evaluated only in release validation (the gated at-scale tests), never on a noisy per-PR runner; 0 waives it (with a reason). `max_peak_heap_mib` is a hard OOM-boundary cap, also anchor-profile / release-validation only. Ceilings are set generously above the measured baseline so only an order-of-magnitude regression trips them. Changing a number here is a deliberate, reviewed edit that MUST update the sibling `reason`. Full policy: docs/development/perf-budgets.md.

cadence.list_overdue.reason: Dashboard/cadence widget, on the home screen's load path. One indexed query (~15us measured). 200ms is a >10,000x margin — it only fires if the query stops using its index entirely.

contact_create.reason: Interactive: the contact form's submit. Query count (8, incl. the fire-and-forget webhook lookup) is the real gate; 500ms wall-clock is ~500x the ~1ms measured median, loose enough for a cold -race runner but well under the ~1s a person reads as a hang on a save.

contact_detail.reason: Interactive: the contact drawer opens on every row click. Query count pinned at the #469 baseline (25) — a new preload that N+1s here is the classic regression this catches. 300ms is ~90x the 3.4ms measured median and an order of magnitude under the ~1s stall threshold.

contact_detail.pathological.reason: Same handler as contact_detail, measured against the awkward manifest record (duplicate keywords, many repeatable fields). A slow contact_detail is usually the pathological one, so it gets the same 300ms interactive ceiling.

contact_list.filtered_sorted.reason: Interactive: the main contact list with a circle filter + sort applied. One query, page-limited result. 300ms is ~18x the 16ms measured median; a filtered sort that stopped hitting an index would blow past it.

contact_list.plain.reason: Interactive: the default contact list — the first screen after login. One query, 50-row page. 300ms is a ~800x margin over the sub-millisecond median; effectively only a full-table-scan regression trips it.

contact_merge.reason: Interactive but not latency-critical: an explicit admin action with a confirmation step, run once. 100 queries (the dependent-table walk) is the gate. 1500ms wall-clock is ~100x the 15ms measured median — generous because merge legitimately does a lot of work.

contact_update.reason: Interactive: the contact form's save on an existing record. 11 queries is the gate; 500ms is ~300x the 1.7ms median, matching contact_create's save-latency ceiling.

dashboard.reason: Interactive: the home screen. 8 fixed aggregate queries is the gate. 300ms is ~230x the 1.3ms median; a dashboard tile that started iterating contacts would trip it.

delete_cascade.reason: Interactive but not latency-critical: an explicit delete with a confirmation, run once. The 35-query manual cascade (CLAUDE.md backend trap #6) is the gate. 1000ms is ~130x the 7.5ms median — loose because a cascade touches many tables by design.

duplicates.find_pairs.reason: WAIVED. Background maintenance feeding a review surface — never on an interactive request path. Already a recorded super-linear finding (#469): its pair count is O(cluster^2). The deterministic budget (query count 5, result size at the baseline) still applies; wall-clock stays a trend signal only.

fts.contact_list_search.reason: Interactive: the contact-list search box. One FTS5 query. 300ms is ~250x the 1.2ms median; a search that fell back off the FTS index to a LIKE scan would trip it.

fts.search_all.reason: Interactive: the global search across contacts/notes/activities. Three FTS5 queries (one per corpus). 300ms is ~350x the 858us median.

graph.traverse_deep.reason: WAIVED. Opt-in deep relationship traversal, not on a default screen. The PERF-01 profiles deliberately scale graph density (hubs, fan-out, chain depth) faster than contact count, so the 2.2s at typical is fixture depth, not a regression. Query count (2 — a recursive CTE, not an N+1) is the property under test. Trend signal only.

graph.traverse_hub.reason: WAIVED. Density-scaled exactly like graph.traverse_deep (315ms at typical is the hub's fan-out in the fixture). Query count (2) is the gate; wall-clock is a trend signal only.

graph.traverse_shallow.reason: Interactive: the 1-hop relationship view on the contact page. Query count (2) is the gate. 500ms (looser than the 300ms reads because result size grows with local density by design) is ~90x the 5.3ms median.

reachout.detect.reason: Interactive: the reach-out suggestions strip. Five bounded queries. 300ms is ~1,000x the 285us median.

backup.vacuum_into.reason: VACUUM INTO runs entirely inside SQLite; Go holds nothing (41 KiB measured peak). 32 MiB is the floor ceiling — anything approaching it means the backup path started buffering the database in Go memory.

delete_cascade.hub.reason: The dependent-table walk issues SQL DELETEs; rows are not loaded (1.2 MiB measured). 32 MiB floor ceiling catches a cascade that started SELECT-ing whole tables into memory before deleting.

duplicates.find_pairs.reason: Recorded super-linear peak-memory finding (#470): it expands O(cluster^2) candidate pairs in memory (12.8 MiB at typical). Capped in the product (it is a review surface, not an unbounded job). 64 MiB is ~5x the measured typical peak — a regression past the known shape trips it; the cross-scale growth-class gate in PERF-03 owns the shape itself.

export.bundle.reason: ExportData builds one bytes.Buffer for the whole multi-section dump before the first byte is sent (linear, expected — 27 MiB at typical). 128 MiB is ~4.5x the measured typical peak; an export that also duplicated the buffer, or stopped freeing per-record scratch, would trip it well before OOM on a 512 MiB box.

export.jscontact.reason: Same whole-result buffering as export.bundle (21 MiB at typical), JSContact serialization. Same 128 MiB OOM-boundary ceiling.

export.vcard4.reason: Same whole-result buffering as export.bundle (21 MiB at typical), vCard 4 serialization. Same 128 MiB OOM-boundary ceiling.

fts.rebuild.reason: INSERT ... SELECT into the FTS5 virtual table inside SQLite; Go holds nothing (23 KiB measured). 32 MiB floor ceiling catches a rebuild that started reading rows into Go to re-index them.

import.vcf.reason: Recorded super-linear peak-memory finding (#470): ParseVCF holds the whole parsed batch and the preview pass is O(n^2) in the row count (20 MiB at typical). Capped in the product at services.MaxVCFContacts. 96 MiB is ~4.5x the measured typical peak — a regression past the known shape trips it; PERF-03's growth-class gate owns the shape.

restore.snapshot.reason: Streams the snapshot file back into place (218 KiB measured peak). 32 MiB floor ceiling catches a restore that started loading the snapshot into memory.
